theme: यज्ञ, अन्न, और नैतिक जीवन-चक्र / Sacrifice, nourishment, and the ethical cycle of life
context: Krishna is clarifying that action can be transformed from self-centered grasping into a sacred offering. In the immediate flow of the chapter, he is moving from the problem of attachment to the practical discipline of living in harmony with the world, where food, sacrifice, and duty are not isolated acts but a shared moral ecology.
contextHindi: कृष्ण यह स्पष्ट कर रहे हैं कि कर्म को स्वार्थ की भूख से निकालकर पूजा की विधि में बदला जा सकता है। अध्याय के तुरंत बाद के प्रसंग में वह यह समझा रहे हैं कि जीवन का अन्न, यज्ञ, और कर्तव्य अलग-अलग काम नहीं, बल्कि एक साझा नैतिक चक्र हैं।
sanskritDevanagari:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः |
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ||३-१३||
transliteration:
yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .
bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt ||3-13||

wordByWord.meaning: what remains after sacrifice; food that has been shared in the spirit of offering
those who eat; those who consume
the righteous, the balanced, those living in inner harmony
from all impurities, burdens, and accumulated faults
for one's own sake; from self-centered motive
the sinful, the morally entangled, the ones living in self-enclosure

spokenHindi: यह श्लोक बहुत सीधी जीवन-शिक्षा देता है: ‘यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तः’—जो लोग यज्ञ के बाद बचे हुए अन्न को ग्रहण करते हैं, वे सभी पापों से मुक्त होते हैं। इसका अर्थ यह नहीं है कि एक विशेष पूजा का पात्र ही पवित्र है, बल्कि यह है कि अगर खाया, लिया, और जीने का तरीका ‘सबके लिए’ और ‘उपहार’ जैसा है, तो मन का अहंकार कम होता है। दूसरी ओर, ‘ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्’—जो लोग अपने लिए ही पकाते हैं, अपने लिए ही खाते हैं, वे पाप खाते हैं, यानी वे अपने जीवन को छोटे स्वार्थ से भरते हैं। इस श्लोक का संदेश है: भोजन, काम, और धन—ये सब एक नैतिक दायित्व भी हैं। अगर हम अपने चारों ओर के जीवन को अलग नहीं मानते, तो किसी भी छोटी-सी क्रिया में भी अहंकार आ जाता है।
clearEnglish: TEXT: The verse says that the righteous who eat what remains from sacrifice are freed from all sins, while those who cook only for themselves are eating sin. This is not a statement about food being magically pure or impure; it is a teaching about motive, circulation, and responsibility. The language of yajña here is wider than ritual fire: it includes the whole pattern of receiving through a larger order and returning with gratitude. INFERENCE: If our nourishment and consumption are organized only around personal gain, the mind becomes enclosed and self-centered. If we see the world as shared, then eating, earning, and serving become moral acts rather than mere transactions. The verse does not prescribe a rigid rule for every plate; it insists that a human being is not isolated from the web of life. The more we consume without a sense of reciprocity, the more we become trapped in selfishness.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse literally distinguishes between those who live in a spirit of offering and those who live for personal consumption alone. It connects ethical life with how food, sharing, and effort are used.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A reasonable conclusion is that ethical living is not only about ritual correctness; it is about reducing greed, recognizing interdependence, and becoming less closed around the self.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: Traditional readings often expand yajña into a wider sense of duty, generosity, and sacred reciprocity. This is useful, but the verse itself remains the primary authority and does not reduce the teaching to any single ritual formula.

practicalApplication.label: Shared nourishment
practicalApplication.text: Before or after eating, briefly acknowledge where the food came from and how it was made. Notice whether the meal is merely a personal convenience or also a shared act of care.

practicalApplication.label: Daily offering
practicalApplication.text: Choose one task—work, study, money, or service—and consciously do it in a way that benefits more than just the self, even slightly, instead of only seeking personal gain.

reflectionQuestion: How do I consume, earn, and act when I am thinking only about my own need, and how could I shift toward shared responsibility without self-condemnation?
reflectionQuestionHindi: जब मैं सिर्फ अपने लाभ के बारे में सोचता हूँ, तो मैं खाना, कमाना और काम करना कैसे करता हूँ? बिना आत्म-निंदा के, मैं इस सोच को साझा जिम्मेदारी की तरफ कैसे ले जा सकता हूँ?
